output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mainly a Brackenford problem, not a Haverlow one. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (week 31), night pallets wait a median of about 3h50 on an unrefrigerated dock (15–17°C) instead of 44 minutes. Haverlow's own trailer telematics show product at 2.4–3.5°C when doors opened, and trailers were empty by about 23:00–23:40. Yet receipt probes were keyed at 02:30–03:20 and read 6.6–7.9°C, so they measure dock warming, not the supplier. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shift stayed flat. Chambers held temperature. Do not raise the chargeback or shift volume, and do not drop the probe. Restore night receiving staffing, or otherwise guarantee fast put-away, and set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly. Separately, ask Corriebank for claim-level data to size over-claiming. Its credits rose after self-certification, but that link is unproven. Confidence is high on the dock cause and moderate on the credits question.
